after: ## Describing a transfer: store, pathway, store
alt: Six energy transfers written as chains. A torch: chemical store of the battery, electrically to the lamp, then by radiation and heating to the surroundings. A rising ball: kinetic to gravitational store. A kettle, a bow, braking and snapping magnets follow the same pattern.
caption: Name the store energy leaves, the pathway, and the store it ends up in.

alt: Two bars split into useful and wasted parts. A lamp: 80 J of 200 J is useful light, 40% efficient, 120 J wasted. A 35% efficient power station delivering 700 MJ has a total of 2000 MJ, so 1300 MJ is wasted.
caption: Useful and wasted parts always add up to the total.

alt: A Sankey diagram on squared paper with 1 square = 10 J. A 400 J input arrow, 40 squares wide, splits into a useful 260 J arrow to the kinetic store of the load (26 squares) and two wasted arrows bending down: 90 J heating (9 squares) and 50 J sound (5 squares).
caption: Arrow widths are to scale and the outputs add up to the input: efficiency 65%.

alt: Conduction: particles in a heated bar vibrate and pass energy along by collisions. Convection: warm fluid rises above a flame and cooler fluid sinks, making a loop. Radiation: a hot object sends infrared waves that can cross a vacuum.
caption: Conduction needs contact, convection needs a fluid, radiation needs neither.

alt: A room with a heater: warm air rises, crosses the ceiling, cools and sinks on the far side, and flows back along the floor. A sea breeze: air over the warmer land rises and cooler air from over the sea moves in, so the breeze blows from sea to land.
caption: Use the full density chain and say where the fluid rises and where it sinks.

alt: Three experiments. Conduction: metal rods heated at one end with pins fixed by wax; the pin falls first from the best conductor. Convection: a dye crystal heated in water traces a loop. Radiation: a hot-water cube emits most infrared from its matt black face and least from its shiny silver face.
caption: Change one thing at a time: the material, the heating position, or the surface.

alt: Cross-section of a vacuum flask with labels: a vacuum between double walls stops conduction and convection, silvered inner surfaces reflect infrared, a plastic or cork stopper is a poor conductor and stops convection, and insulating supports reduce conduction.
caption: Each feature of a vacuum flask tackles a different method of energy transfer.
